headline: Independent Director  |  Investment Committee Member  |  African Markets

location.linkedinText: South Africa

about:
Most investment committees share one feature. The person who has actually built and exited the kind of business under discussion is rarely the person sitting at the table.

I have spent thirty years on the operating side of African markets - building businesses, integrating acquisitions, navigating regulators, and selling to institutional buyers. I now sit on the other side of the table. Boards. Investment committees. Advisory mandates. My work is to ask the questions the deal team has stopped asking and to hold the line when a room talks itself into a decision the numbers do not support.

Today I serve as Strategic Advisor, Non-Executive Director, and Project Owner across financial services, governance, and impact capital mandates. I advise institutional capital partners on fund formation, governance, and portfolio strategy across Africa, the GCC, and Europe, with active engagement across pan-African venture and advisory platforms.

Earlier, I was Principal at Renew Capital, Chief Executive Officer of a diversified African conglomerate, and founder-CEO of a group I built over two decades.

I take independent seats selectively. The discipline of saying no to most invitations is what gives weight to the seats I hold.

Based in Pretoria. Active across Addis Ababa, Nairobi, Kigali, Amsterdam, and New York.

headline: Founder & Managing Partner @ KHOLO CAPITAL (R1,4 billion Mezzanine Debt Fund) - SA, Botswana, Namibia, Swaziland & Lesotho

location.linkedinText: City of Johannesburg, Gauteng, South Africa

about:
Mokgome Mogoba is an experienced Investment Banker, Fund Manager and Deal Maker with an investment track record of more than 24yrs.

He is the Founder & Managing Partner of Kholo Capital a R1,4 billion Mezzanine Debt fund. We provide mezzanine debt loan funding R70m to R205m to medium sized businesses that generate minimum R25m annual EBITDA per annum in all sectors (excluding primary mining and primary farming). We provide growth capital & acquisition funding to businesses in SA, Botswana, Namibia, Swaziland and Lesotho. Investment tenor 4 to 7yrs targeting returns above 17% (interest rate plus equity upside).

Shareholder and former partner at Vantage Capital. He originated, structured, executed and actively managed investments in many markets and assisted with fundraising raising R11bn across 4 private credit funds (2 Mezzanine Debt and 2 Renewable Energy senior debt funds). He led the conclusion and successful exits of the New GX, Thebe Timrite and Efekto investments and the conclusion of the Rosslyn Riviera shopping mall (Kenya) and Simba Properties (Uganda) investments and also oversaw the investment in Primedia.

Whilst at Standard Bank Corporate and Investment Banking, Mokgome was the Head of the Financial Institutions Group, BEE and Public Sector divisions for a number of years whereby he concluded more than R25bn of investments. These include providing R2bn of growth capital to Old Mutual Finance, providing R2bn of investment capital to Shanduka Group (now Phembani), and concluding $400m debt advisory mandate for Kenya Airways. 

Mokgome was a member of Standard Bank’s Private Equity team and also a founding member of the Mezzanine Debt investment team in 2005 whereby he co-led the conclusion of a number of investments. These include arranging and underwriting Mezzanine Debt and Senior Debt funding transactions including R6.9bn to fund the Sasol Group (Inzalo) BEE transaction, R6.2bn to fund the De Beers Ponahalo BEE transaction, R800m to fund the WACO Leveraged Buyout by JP Morgan Partners, R350m Metrofile’s restructured debt, R600m to fund Phembani’s acquisition of a 20% stake in Engen and R1.5bn to fund the Sasol Oil (Tshwarisano) BEE transaction.

Mokgome also built the Private Equity Buyout/Leverage Finance, Optimal Capital structuring and Credit rating models at Standard Bank and provided training and induction to staff across the whole bank.

Mokgome is a qualified Chartered Accountant and holds a BCom (Acc) degree Summa Cum Laude where he came first in the Faculty of Commerce, Law & Mgt. He’s also a member of SA Institute of Directors.

currentPosition.description:
R1,4 billion KHOLO CAPITAL MEZZANINE DEBT FUND

Please keep us in mind whenever equity funding is needed we can plug the equity funding gap with mezzanine debt loan funding (subordinated loans) so shareholders don’t give up too much equity & don’t suffer too much equity dilution.

We provide mezzanine debt funding R70m to R205m to medium sized businesses generating min R25m EBITDA in all sectors (excl primary mining, resources, primary agri, gambling, ammunition, hard liquor & tobacco). However, we can fund mining services/products, mining logistics/transportation, mineral processing & Agri-processing. We can arrange larger ticket sizes also.

We provide growth capital & acquisition funding to medium sized businesses with operations in SA, Botswana, Namibia, Swaziland or Lesotho. Investment tenor 4 to 7yrs targeting returns above 17% (interest rate plus equity upside). Leverage up to 3,5x to 4x Total Debt (senior and mezz debt) to EBITDA or up to 80% LTV.

We fund share buy backs, refinancing of shareholder loans & dividend recaps. We also fund management buyouts, leveraged buyouts and private equity buyouts.

We can also pay down portion of senior debt funding especially where the senior debt has steep capital repayments, in order to create cashflow headroom for the business. Mezzanine debt loan funding is typically 5-6yr bullet loan funding with capital repayable right at the end on the maturity of the loan. The business only has to service interest payments during the loan tenor thereby creating Cashflow headroom and the business can re-invest the excess cashflows for growth. 

Business must be generating min R25m EBITDA at the time of investment. So we can’t fund new developments on a ring fenced basis. We can look at greenfield opportunities provided there is a guarantee from a business that generates the min R25m EBITDA. The guarantee can fall away once the business meets thresholds and covenants are met. Also, we can’t fund distressed assets or turnarounds.

headline: Purpose: Africa’s Sustainability. Building Shared Value through the private sector, shifting leadership mindsets, advancing ESG and driving profitable solutions to societal challenges.

location.linkedinText: City of Johannesburg, Gauteng, South Africa

about:
Founder & CEO | Shared Value Africa | Shift Impact Africa
Over the past decade, I have built Shared Value Africa into a pan-African platform working with the private sector to move beyond ESG commitments to real value creation. Where profitability and societal progress are designed together, not traded off.

Through Shared Value Africa, I have established a presence across more than 12 countries, convening business leaders, institutions, and partners to embed Shared Value into strategy, leadership, research, and training. The focus is clear: to shift how business is done in Africa so that it creates value for all stakeholders while strengthening long-term competitiveness.

Alongside this, Shift Impact Africa develops platforms that enable entrepreneurs and SMEs to participate more meaningfully in Africa’s economic future. This includes initiatives such as JamiiTrade, designed to unlock intra-African trade and expand access to markets for growing businesses.

A core pillar of my work is advancing gender equality and workplace safety , not as a compliance requirement, but as a business and economic imperative. Through research, training, and partnerships, we work with organisations to better understand risk, strengthen workplace practices, and build more inclusive and productive environments.

My work sits at the intersection of business, society, and leadership , contributing to how organisations think, operate, and grow across the continent.
Focus areas:
• Shared Value as a business strategy
• ESG foundations and accountability
• Gender equality and addressing GBVH in the workplace
• Entrepreneurship and SME ecosystems
• Private sector leadership and systems change

Africa’s future will not be shaped by intention, but by action.
The question is whether we are building systems that allow the continent to create value for itself.

currentPosition.description: As the Founder and CEO of Shared Value Africa, my vision is to transform the African business landscape by embedding the principles of profit with purpose into core business strategy. I am committed to advancing a new leadership mindset—one that prioritizes ethical governance, inclusive growth, and long-term sustainability. My role spans advocacy, strategy development, ecosystem building, and driving impact across the continent through initiatives that support entrepreneurs, empower women, and promote responsible business practices. Our focus is on entrepreneurs, empowering women through advocating for gender equality, and shifting business leadership mindsets towards taking up the responsibility of ensuring prosperity for all stakeholders. Together with our partners, we are working to position Africa as the global leader in creating shared value.

projects.title: Shared Value Africa Gender Equality  Unit
projects.description:
Building on our extensive work in Gender Equality, including our research and collaboration with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) on the Respect@Work program, I recognized the need to create a dedicated Gender Equality Unit. This unit serves as a centralized platform to consolidate all our efforts, insights, and initiatives aimed at advancing gender equality and addressing workplace harassment.

The Gender Equality Unit was launched to not only amplify our impact but also to send a clear message to businesses: failing to address gender inequality and harassment poses significant risks, both ethically and economically. By providing tools, training, and advisory support, the unit helps organizations recognize that fostering inclusive and respectful workplaces is not just a moral imperative but a business-critical issue. Through this initiative, we aim to drive systemic change by equipping businesses to take proactive measures, mitigate risks, and embrace the value of equality in creating sustainable, thriving workplaces.

projects.title: JamiiTrade
projects.description:
In 2021, university students conducted research to evaluate African entrepreneurs’ understanding of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) and its potential for creating new markets. The findings revealed a significant knowledge gap, highlighting the need for accessible resources to help entrepreneurs leverage AfCFTA’s opportunities effectively. This insights inspired me to drive the conceptualisation and the creation of JamiiTrade, a platform aimed at empowering African entrepreneurs.

Currently in its beta phase, JamiiTrade began with the development of its website, designed in collaboration with a digital expert. The platform addresses key challenges by providing critical information, capacity-building tools, and research insights to enable entrepreneurs to navigate cross-border trade and access new markets.

JamiiTrade also fosters collaboration through a peer-to-peer learning environment, allowing entrepreneurs to share knowledge, build networks, and explore opportunities for growth. While still in its early stages, the platform is positioned to become a vital resource for driving intra-African trade and supporting the next generation of African business leaders in unlocking the full potential of AfCFTA.

projects.title: African Universities Gender Equality Forum
projects.description: I conceptualized, developed, and with the support of my team,  implemented the Africa Universities Gender Equality Online Forum, driven by my strong belief in the vital role academic institutions play in combating Gender-Based Violence and Harassment. This platform was created to foster collaboration and dialogue among universities across Africa, enabling them to share initiatives and strategies for addressing gender inequality and harassment on campuses and in classrooms. Since 2021, we have successfully hosted two African Universities Gender Equality Forums online each year, amplifying the conversation and inspiring action toward a more equitable academic environment.

projects.title: Shared Value Africa Academy
projects.description: In March 2021, together with my team, I developed the Shared Value Africa Academy, a dedicated platform designed to centralize and deliver all Shared Value training programs. The Academy serves as a comprehensive hub for equipping businesses, organizations, and individuals with the tools, knowledge, and strategies to implement the Shared Value business model effectively. Through tailored training modules, workshops, and resources, the Academy empowers participants to align their strategies with societal impact, fostering sustainable growth and addressing pressing social challenges. This initiative reflects our commitment to driving transformative change across Africa by building capacity and embedding the principles of Shared Value into the core of business operations.

projects.title: CEO CONNECT FORUM
projects.description:
At Shared Value Africa, we recognized that leadership plays a pivotal role in driving sustainability across the African continent and improving the lives of its people. Strong, ethical leadership is essential for fostering innovative solutions to the continent's unique challenges and unlocking its immense potential. With this vision, we conceptualized the Shared Value Africa CEO Connect Forum, a platform designed to bring together influential business leaders, policymakers, and thought leaders from across Africa. The forum serves as a catalyst for collaboration, knowledge-sharing, and actionable commitments toward building a sustainable and inclusive future.

Since its inception, the Shared Value Africa CEO Connect Forum has been successfully delivered in various countries, focusing on key topics such as sustainable economic growth, gender equality, climate action, entrepreneurship, and the integration of Shared Value principles into core business strategies. To date, we have hosted eight impactful forums, each tailored to address the pressing needs and opportunities in the respective regions. These gatherings have facilitated meaningful dialogue, fostered partnerships, and inspired leaders to embrace Shared Value as a framework for creating both economic success and societal impact. Through this initiative, we continue to drive the conversation on responsible leadership and its role in shaping a prosperous and equitable Africa.

projects.title: African Entrepreneurship Forum
projects.description: Through our work at Shared Value Africa, where one of our key target audiences includes entrepreneurs, start-ups, and young businesses, I recognized the need to create a platform that empowers these young individuals to connect, collaborate, and grow collectively. This platform was designed to facilitate peer-to-peer communication, provide valuable information, and foster mutual learning. Since its launch in 2020, we have successfully hosted four online forums annually, driving engagement and knowledge-sharing among emerging business leaders.

projects.title: Gender Based Violence #Itsnotok Movement
projects.description: In 2020, during the height of the COVID-19 pandemic, the world—and South Africa in particular—witnessed a disturbing rise in Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and femicide. The pandemic not only exposed the deep-seated inequalities in our society but also amplified the vulnerabilities of women and children who faced heightened risks while confined to their homes. In response to this alarming trend, we launched the #ItsNotOk movement, a call to action aimed at raising awareness, fostering dialogue, and driving meaningful change to combat GBV and femicide. This movement has since grown into a powerful platform for advocacy, education, and community mobilization, addressing the urgent need for systemic solutions to end gender-based violence.

projects.title: Africa Export Competitiveness Report
projects.description:
In 2022, inspired by the transformative potential of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) to unlock new markets and drive economic growth across the continent, I initiated the idea of exploring how we could actively support its implementation. Recognizing the value of a collaborative approach, I partnered with Dr. Amit Kapoor from Shared Value India to develop a comprehensive research strategy aimed at identifying key opportunities and challenges within AfCFTA.

Together, we embarked on an in-depth research project, leveraging our collective expertise to provide actionable insights for businesses and policymakers. This collaboration culminated in the release of the 2023 Africa Continental Free Trade Area Report, which we proudly launched in Ghana in partnership with the African Capacity Building Foundation. The report serves as a crucial resource for empowering stakeholders to maximize the benefits of AfCFTA while fostering inclusive trade and economic development across Africa.

projects.title: Gender Equality Research
projects.description:
In 2021, I spearheaded a research project focused on analyzing female representation at senior leadership levels within companies listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, specifically in the financial services sector. The study aimed to uncover disparities in gender representation, highlight areas for improvement, and provide actionable insights for fostering greater diversity and inclusion at the top levels of corporate decision-making.

Building on this commitment to addressing gender inequality, in 2022, I collaborated with Professor Corne Davis from the University of Johannesburg to produce the groundbreaking research report titled "The Costly Impact of Gender-Based Violence (GBV)." This report delved into the far-reaching economic and social consequences of GBV, offering a compelling case for the private sector to take proactive measures in addressing this critical issue. Together, these research initiatives reflect my dedication to driving systemic change by addressing both gender equity in leadership and the broader societal challenges that impact workplaces and communities.

The Young Heroes of Swaziland program gathers funds from sponsors to distribute to Swazi orphan children under the age of 18. Unlike other programs, our goal is to keep families together on their homesteads and in their communities. So, instead of supporting one individual child, your contribution goes towards helping the entire family meet its basic needs. You can sponsor a family either in whole or in part. (Because some families are large, it often takes more than one sponsor to support them.) 

The devastation of AIDS is creating a generation of orphans in Swaziland. Though it's one of the smallest of all countries, Swaziland has the world's highest rate of HIV/AIDS infection. According to the 2012 HIV Incidence Measurement Survey, 31% of adults ages 18 to 49 have HIV.

Because of that, nearly 125,000 Swazi children have lost at least one parent to the epidemic. The country's orphans struggle every day for the bare necessities of life. The number of these young heroes is growing daily. Already, over 15,000 households in the country are headed by children who are trying to raise their little brothers and sisters by themselves.

Now, you can help them. For as little as US$20 per month, your organization, your class, your family or you alone can sponsor an orphan family through YoungHeroes.org.sz. Your support will help keep these children's families together and bring them the crucial food, clothing and education they need.

Just as important, you'll give them hope by letting them know that someone cares.

Young Heroes is underwritten and operated by NERCHA, the National Emergency Response Council on HIV/AIDS of the government of Swaziland. It was created with the help of U.S. Peace Corps.

location.linkedinText: City of Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa

about:
I work at the intersection of private markets, strategic relationships, and capital that needs to be matched intelligently.

My primary focus is bridging family office capital and institutional capital in situations where fit, alignment, and process quality matter as much as the opportunity itself.

At Kadenwood, I spend my time connecting the right situations with the right counterparties across family offices, private equity, hedge funds, UHNWI circles, and broader institutional buyers. I am especially drawn to opportunities where the capital on the other side needs to be curated rather than simply contacted.

My background spans capital markets, M&A, venture capital, and growth-oriented businesses, with prior experience as a fund manager raising capital across real assets and alternative sectors. That mix has shaped how I think about markets: access matters, but judgment matters more.

I’m particularly focused on:
 - bridging family offices and institutional capital
 - high-conviction secondaries
 - GP-led and structured liquidity situations
 - bespoke cross-border capital solutions
 - buyer curation, process design, and strategic relationship building

At Kadenwood, we combine independent advisory, senior-led execution, deep relationships across family offices and institutional investors, and a cross-border platform designed for complex capital markets work.
I use this page to share observations on family offices, institutional capital, secondaries, market structure, buyer behavior, and how sophisticated counterparties think about quality.

If you work across family offices, private equity, hedge funds, secondaries, or strategic private capital, I’m always open to thoughtful conversations.

headline: Founder of Critical Metals PLC

location.linkedinText: South Africa

about:
Russell is a seasoned executive & fund manager with over 30 years of expertise in natural resources, developing markets, & commodities. Russell is a Founder, Creator, and Builder of businesses with unsurpassed experience in metals & mining investing. Previously he was the CEO & Executive Chairman of Critical Metals Plc, a company he founded in 2018. Critical Metals focused on acquiring & developing brownfield mining & metals projects, particularly in critical metals, with its key asset in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Russell brings 18 years of experience in the DRC region, driving the company’s long-term strategic goals.

He is the founder of Baobab Physical Commodities & Baobab Asset Management. As Chief Investment Officer of Baobab Physical Commodities since 2015, Russell has led global trading in non-ferrous & precious minerals, specialising in off-take agreements & investments across Africa, Latin America, Central America, Asia, & Europe. Since 2009, as CIO of Baobab Asset Management, he has advised mining, agricultural, & industrial companies in emerging & developed markets, offering strategic insights into capital market strategies in North America and Europe.

In 2014,Russell co-founded Western Uranium Corp. (CSE: WUC), where he spearheaded early strategic growth, key mergers and acquisitions, & positioning the company as a leader in vanadium and uranium. As Executive Chairman in 2017, he focused on expanding the company’s leadership in critical minerals within the USA.

Russell’s financial career includes senior roles at top institutions. As Divisional Director at Macquarie Group, he led equity sales in South African equities & metals/mining for European & North American markets, leveraging international finance expertise to build lasting relationships. 

At North Sound Capital, a $3 billion hedge fund, he managed the global metals & mining investments, delivering strong returns amid market volatility.

Earlier roles include Director of Emerging Markets at Deutsche Bank AG, where he advanced African equities distribution & equity capital market activities, and at HSBC South Africa, where he honed expertise in global commodities trading. His career began at Robert Fleming & Co., where he played a pivotal role in listing Billiton (now BHP) on the London Stock Exchange, marking the start of his focus on metals & mining equities.

Russell was a Director at the Critical Minerals Institute (CMI) until August 2025, contributing his extensive leadership, strategic insights, & industry expertise to advance the critical minerals sector globally.

headline: Debunking misleading leadership advise | 25 years in senior leadership and still learning.

location.linkedinText: Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa

about:
Leadership advice is broken.
 
After 25 years in senior leadership, I’ve learned that much of the advice leaders are given sounds great on a whiteboard but falls apart when the building is actually burning.
 
“Communicate more.”
 
“Empower your people.”
 
“Be vulnerable.”
 
“Lead with empathy.”
 
All good principles.
 
But what happens when you have to make an unpopular decision?
 
When someone you value is underperforming?
 
When your team is losing confidence?
 
When the business is under pressure and there are no good options?
 
That’s where leadership gets real.
 
I write about the gap between leadership advice and leadership reality — challenging the clichés, questioning the guru wisdom and sharing lessons from 25 years of leading people and businesses through difficult situations.
 
I don't believe there is one leadership style that works in every situation.
 
I believe your values are your compass.
 
How you lead yourself matters.
 
How you behave when nobody is watching matters.
 
How you treat people when you're under pressure matters.
 
And ultimately, leadership isn't about having all the answers.
 
It's about having the courage to make the decisions that need to be made, taking responsibility for the consequences, and bringing people with you.
 
My content is for leaders who are tired of performative leadership and want something that actually works in the real world.
  
That's how I approach leadership advice.
 
And that's what you'll find here.

headline: Fractional Transport MD | Chaired 3 BEE JVs — Anglo Zimele, AfriSam, Tongaat-Hulett | 20+ years as MD: Unitrans, DHL, Imperial, SABOT | Member IoDSA

location.linkedinText: City of Johannesburg, Gauteng, South Africa

about:
I am a fractional executive. I advise and I execute.
 
I fix transport businesses. And I design and build BEE deals for Tier 1 contracts — the model, the costings, the funding, the operation behind it.
 
Twenty one years as a Managing Director — Unitrans, DHL, Imperial, SABOT — with MD responsibility across ten SADC countries and operational experience in twelve. Eleven companies acquired across those thirty years. At Unitrans I ran the Freight Division, chaired five Tier 1 joint ventures — three of them empowerment structures: Klipstone with Holcim (now AfriSam), Nomakanjani with Anglo Zimele, and a Small Cane Growers venture with Tongaat-Hulett — and was one of three MDs retained to restructure thirteen regional subsidiaries into three industry silos.
 
Transport businesses struggle for many reasons. The trick is diagnosing the real one quickly — and most often it's that nobody can match cost to revenue, per lane, per vehicle, per entity. So the losses hide, and everyone argues about the wrong thing.
 
I find them, and I don't soften it. Sometimes the answer an owner needs is that the contract in front of him will bankrupt him. Better he hears that before he signs it than in year two, when the trucks are bought and the lane is losing money on every load.
 
HOW TO ENGAGE ME
 
Days, not deliverables. Two days a week, or three days a month — whatever the problem needs. Most clients start with one thing that won't move: a deal that won't fund, a business that won't report, an acquisition they can't price. Most of them keep me on afterwards.
 
I am the MD you can't afford to employ fulltime.
 
Board member, Road Freight Association, 2000–2005.
 
fil@sadclogisticsadvisors.com · +27 82 326 9416

currentPosition.description:
BEE Tier 1 contract enablement. For operators holding a contract but no capital. Transport costing, fleet configuration, OEM facilitation, and a three-statement model and funding pack to DFI standard — then the transaction structured so funders can say yes, with the diligence done before it reaches their desk.
 
Turnaround and diagnostics. Cost per kilometre, per tonne, per lane. Transport P&L per entity. Asset utilisation. Whether the systems report and whether the structure holds. A sequenced list of what to fix first.
 
Acquisitions. Target assessment, valuation, and integration — eleven companies acquired across thirty years, including Unitrans' purchase of Cane Carriers from Tongaat-Hulett, where I ran the Zululand integration.
 
Restructures. Unitrans: thirteen regional subsidiaries across six countries consolidated into three industry-focused silos — one of three MDs retained to implement it.
 
Fractional execution and governance. Operational setup as your fractional executive; post-launch oversight as a non-executive director with covenant responsibility.
 
#Road freight · #Cross-border logistics · #SADC corridors · #BEE transport development

The Forest Products business unit integrated the inbound logistics chain to paper mills including cilviculture, harvesting, extraction, loading, transportation and mill yard management.
The business had a geographical market focus supplying largely bulk transportation services to the Forestry, Fuel, Mining and Sugar industries.
The company in 1994 provided transportation services to mainly the Mining and Fuel industries in Zululand. Marketing efforts resulted in significant growth in the timber and sugar cane industries.

This company (now Supply Chain Services - Fuel Group) was acquired by South African Breweries with a view to establish a distribution channel to Supermarkets and Convenience stores, additional to the traditional liquor retail market. The company provided warehousing, distribution, sales, merchandising and factoring services to 32 principles in the FMCG industry. Key statistics; 2 mother warehouses, 8 redistributor warehouses, circa 1 450 SKUs and 8 600 stores accounts.

Direct accountability for road transportation services to multiple customers in the Forestry, Freight, Fuel, Mining, Paper and Sugar industries.

Comprehensive overview and exposure to all financial departments including Accounts, Capital Control, Management Accounts, Procurement, Stores and Time Office.

I collaborate closely with our Chief Commercial Officer to identify, analyze, and prioritize strategic opportunities with asset managers, brokers, market makers, fintechs, retail banks, and regulators. My role involves working with both internal and external parties to execute the operational requirements and ensuring these opportunities are commercially beneficial for all involved.

With a decade of experience spanning finance and technology, my career reflects a commitment to innovation and growth. My journey into the cryptocurrency space began with a passion for alternative financial systems, leading me to co-found a crypto startup dedicated to enhancing decentralized fund storage. Additionally, I conduct technical analysis, research, writing, and consulting for various crypto and tech projects through my private research firm.

At VALR, I leverage my extensive background in finance and technology to foster strategic partnerships that are central to our global expansion efforts. My focus is on forming meaningful connections and ensuring these partnerships align with and advance our strategic business goals, reinforcing VALR's position as a leader in the crypto industry.

VALR is a Pantera-backed international cryptocurrency exchange that offers a comprehensive trading platform that connects global customers to a wide variety of cryptocurrencies and related services. While serving customers globally, VALR is also the largest exchange headquartered in Africa and has deep liquidity against South African Rand (ZAR). We employ state-of-the-art security measures and high-performance proprietary exchange technology to ensure a safe and efficient trading environment. Our products and services include a sophisticated spot and spot margin exchange, futures trading, liquid staking, VALR Pay, OTC trading, a seamless fiat to USDC and EURC minting product, and a world-class API designed to cater to the needs of institutional traders and fintechs. By prioritizing customer support and user experience, VALR aims to democratize access to digital assets, providing a reliable gateway for participants in the cryptocurrency market worldwide.

about:
Fund Administrator & Tracing Agent | Provident Fund Administration | Beneficiary Tracing & Compliance

I have 7 months of experience as a Fund Administrator and Tracing Agent within the Private Security Sector Provident Fund, specialising in death benefit claims, beneficiary tracing, case investigations, and Trustee presentations. In this role, I have successfully presented over 20 cases against a target of 15 and was awarded Best Tracer/Fund Administrator for November.

Prior to this, I gained experience in debt collection through a 1-year learnership at VVM Debt Collectors starting on 6 March 2023. After successfully completing the program, I was offered a permanent contract due to strong performance, developing skills in client engagement, negotiations, compliance, and financial management.

I am skilled in compliance, risk management, stakeholder communication, and managing sensitive cases with accuracy and professionalism. I am motivated by challenges, continuous learning, and making a meaningful impact on people’s lives through my work.

currentPosition.description:
Fund Administrator & Tracing Agent | EasyDebit | PSSPF

I am a dedicated Fund Administrator and Tracing Agent specialising in provident fund death benefit administration and beneficiary tracing within the Private Security Sector Provident Fund (PSSPF). My role focuses on ensuring that benefits are allocated fairly, accurately, and in full compliance with the Pension Funds Act and Fund Rules.

I manage the end-to-end tracing and investigation process, including identifying legal and financial dependants, verifying documentation, resolving disputes, and compiling detailed case reports for presentation to internal review structures and Trustees. I regularly engage with beneficiaries, attorneys, employers, Home Affairs, SALT, the Master’s Office, and third parties to resolve complex cases involving customary marriages, life partnerships, minor dependants, and missing beneficiaries.

Key responsibilities include beneficiary tracing, document verification, compliance checks, case analysis, and Trustee presentations. I handle sensitive matters with professionalism and empathy while maintaining strong governance and risk controls.

Key achievements include:

Successfully presenting over 20 cases in a reporting period, exceeding the target of 15 cases.

Awarded a Certificate for Best Tracer / Fund Administrator – November in recognition of outstanding performance, efficiency, and case quality.

Contributing to reduced case deferrals through proactive document review and case readiness.

Assisting in the resolution of long-standing and complex cases involving disputed dependants and incomplete records.

I am detail-oriented, results-driven, and motivated by making a meaningful impact by ensuring beneficiaries receive what they are legally entitled to while safeguarding fund integrity

about:
Catherine Young has more than 25 years professional, executive level experience as an African entrepreneur across several industries, including a successful corporate career, holding various senior positions in companies including Deloitte, Chevron and SAP, managing multi-million dollar budgets and large teams. She is a Partner at Knife Capital, Founder of SME consulting business, Thinkroom and Managing Partner of Grindstone and Grindstone Ventures. Her capabilities are underpinned by deep engagement and care for people across her work career, with an astute ability to build and grow businesses. Her corporate and franchise experience has been instrumental in shaping her journey as an entrepreneur and investor, enabling her to recognise and cultivate the qualities that lead to business success.

As a Partner at Knife Capital, she plays a key role in growing portfolio companies for exit, with a focus on scaling businesses to maximise value. She is actively involved in deal flow, investment decisions, and portfolio support, ensuring strategic alignment and growth. She also contributes to networking and sourcing high-potential investments, sits on various Investment Committees, and supports Knife as a structured fund management business. Beyond investments, she leads initiatives to optimise portfolio performance, strengthen fund operations, and drive strategic partnerships to enhance the firm’s impact. As founder of Thinkroom, she is involved in entrepreneurial ecosystem development across Africa and have internationalised her businesses. Catherine is an SME ecosystem influencer in Africa and works with clients in the space of entrepreneurship development across the continent. As the Managing Partner of Grindstone, she plays a critical role in developing entrepreneurial ecosystems globally. With a keen understanding of the challenges faced by startups and SMEs. 

Catherine has co-authored various books, and as a renowned authority on entrepreneurship, start-up ecosystems, and ecosystem development, Catherine is also a public speaker and thought leader in the industry. She shares her insights with others through keynote presentations, workshop facilitation, and by chairing ecosystem events. Catherine has also been a speaker invitee to WEF. She holds a Bachelor Degree in Commerce, National Diploma in Procurement and a Venture Finance Certificate from Saïd Business School, University of Oxford. headline: 15+ years in African trade. Now building the financial infrastructure to unlock capital that was always there. Tokenization, RWAs, and the markets everyone else is still figuring out. Blockchain Coach 1:1, Speaker

location.linkedinText: South Africa

about:
I spent my first decade in trade watching money move in one direction.

Brazilian furniture leaving factories in Rio Grande do Sul. Arriving in Cape Town. The manufacturer got paid. The intermediary got paid. The bank got paid. The currency spread got paid. By the time the transaction settled, the original producer had captured a fraction of what the market paid for their product.

I did not study this problem. I lived inside it. Across 45+ countries, across agriculture, minerals, manufactured goods, and financial services.

That pattern never changed. It just took different shapes depending on the country. In West Africa it was groundnuts. In Southern Africa it was copper. In Southeast Asia it was timber. The asset was different. The structure was the same. Value created at the source, captured somewhere else.

I started in Brazil. Export Sales Manager at Moveis Carraro, where I led the commercial department responsible for 30% of revenues and built the international market share from the ground up. Export Excellence Award. Real numbers, real markets, real accountability.

Then Africa. I opened a channel connecting 35 Brazilian suppliers to South African buyers, established a showroom in Cape Town, and drove a 22% increase in sales in 14 months. The Brazilian Consulate became a working partner. So did the furniture sector, the trade networks, and the buyers on both sides of the Atlantic.

Then cybersecurity. VP of Sales at Archistry Incorporated, managing Global 500 accounts across 19 countries. Banking, manufacturing, petrochemicals, financial services. The industries where capital allocation decisions actually get made.

Web3 came next, not as a pivot but as a conclusion. After seeing how capital moves, and who it bypasses, the technology was not the interesting question. The interesting question was: what breaks if you remove the intermediary?

I have been answering that question since 2020. In community, in strategy, in live deals.

Africa is not capital-poor. It is capital-locked. The land, the minerals, the harvests, the infrastructure, the receivables. All of it exists. None of it is currently accessible to global capital in a form that moves at market speed.

Tokenization changes that. Not as a theory. As a mechanism I am building, one asset class at a time.

I work with founders, fund managers, and policymakers who are ready to stop waiting for traditional finance to show up. If that is you, let's talk.

volunteering.description:
Humanitarian Leadership and Global Volunteer

During the early stages of the Russia-Ukraine conflict in February 2022, my longstanding commitment to volunteer work with the Transcendental Meditation Movement brought me to Constanța, Romania, near the Black Sea. Located approximately 146 kilometers (91 miles) from the Ukrainian border, this region became a hub for critical humanitarian efforts, where I played a key leadership role in coordinating support for refugees fleeing the conflict.

I spearheaded negotiations with Romanian, Black Sea based, hotel organizations to secure food and lodging for Ukrainian families, ensuring their safety and comfort during a time of immense upheaval. In parallel, I managed and guided the operational efforts of our volunteer team, fostering collaboration and compassion while addressing the urgent needs of displaced individuals. This chapter of my humanitarian involvement concluded in September 2022, reflecting the natural resolution of my responsibilities related to the conflict.

Beyond this specific mission, my commitment to the Transcendental Meditation Movement continues on a global scale. I provide financial sponsorships to support aspiring Transcendental Meditation teachers, helping them access the 6-month on-campus training program in Chattrakorn, Thailand. Additionally, I dedicate both time and financial resources to initiatives empowering at-risk children, enabling them to learn the Transcendental Meditation technique and offering ongoing mentorship to help them thrive.

Through these efforts, I remain deeply committed to creating positive change by supporting individuals and communities in their journey toward resilience, growth, and well-being.

Since 2012, I have been deeply committed to supporting and empowering emerging African entrepreneurs across diverse industries, including fashion, tech, food and beverage, video streaming content, radio and millinery hat making. Through a philanthropic and mentorship-driven approach, I have provided strategic guidance, industry expertise, and professional insights to help these entrepreneurs navigate challenges and scale their ventures. Additionally, I have actively leveraged my network to create meaningful opportunities, fostering innovation and sustainable growth within these sectors.

My dedication to this initiative reflects my passion for mentorship, capacity-building, and the advancement of entrepreneurial talent, reinforcing my belief in the transformative power of business as a force for positive change.

headline: Specialist Analyst at Financial Sector Conduct Authority

location.linkedinText: City of Johannesburg, Gauteng, South Africa

about:
I’m a Specialist Analyst at the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA), with a strong foundation in regulatory supervision, risk management, and stakeholder engagement. I currently lead the project addressing Section 13A non-compliances, where I oversee the analysis of fund submissions, publish lists of defaulting employers, engage directly with stakeholders, and drive strategic interventions to strengthen compliance across the retirement fund industry.

With a postgraduate diploma in Risk Management and extensive experience in regulatory environments, I bring a strategic and analytical approach to oversight. My work spans supervisory engagements, thematic reviews, complaints resolution, and the preparation of high-impact reports for management and executive committees.

I’m passionate about using data and regulatory insights to drive accountability, protect fund members, and support the integrity of the financial sector. I thrive in collaborative environments, enjoy sharing knowledge, and actively contribute to projects that improve regulatory outcomes.

Let’s connect if you’re interested in governance, risk, compliance, or the evolving landscape of retirement fund supervision.

headline: Academic (Oxford, LSE), Author (Adventure Finance), Advisor (The ImPact, BEAM network, Jumo, Nyala Venture), Angel Investor (Dazzle), Founder (Innovative Finance Initiative, Impact Finance Pro)

location.linkedinText: City of Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa

about:
If you’re planning to connect here, please include a note on how we know each other—whether we’ve collaborated, you’ve been in one of my classes, or we’ve crossed paths in this ecosystem. I don’t accept invitations from people I haven’t engaged with, but you’re welcome to follow me or subscribe to our newsletter at innovative.finance or adventure.finance.

I often describe my work through the 4 As: Academic, Author, Advisor, and Angel Investor.

Academic
At Oxford’s Saïd Business School, I’m an Associate Fellow and Entrepreneur-in-Residence at the Skoll Centre, and a Visiting Fellow at LSE’s Marshall Institute. I design and teach courses on innovative finance, impact investing, and tech for impact—across MBA, EMBA, MCom, MPhil, MLF, and executive education programs. I’ve also built online courses with Coursera and GetSmarter, and serve as Academic Director for the BEAM Network. Beyond Oxford, I guest lecture at institutions around the world.

Author
My first book, Adventure Finance (Palgrave Macmillan, 2021), helps purpose-driven founders and funders navigate their financing options and design funding journeys that fit. Advisor

publications.title: "The Social Investment Market: The Role of Public Policy in Innovation and Execution"
publications.publishedAt: Oxford University & The UK Cabinet Office · Feb 1, 2013
publications.description:
This report, arising from a symposium co-hosted by the University of Oxford and the Cabinet Office in November 2012, captures the reflections of senior policy-makers, investors, advisors, academics and analysts from over ten countries as they discuss the historic and future role of public policy in the social investment market. 
 
During the symposium, the increasing sophistication and scale of the UK social investment market was evidenced, as well as the fact that the innovations in funding intermediaries, legal structures, financial products, tax incentives and government commissioning and procurement act as examples to governments and private entities worldwide.  Sir Ronald Cohen noted that “The Social Investment Symposium was a landmark in the progress of this new, vitally important market. It has set the scene for greater international collaboration…”.

publications.title: The Integration of Social and Environmental Value Flows into the Early-Stage Investment Process
publications.description: Although the concept of blended valuation lies at the heart of triple bottom line investing, funders of social enterprises continue to employ a “check the box” mentality to social impact, deploying investment frameworks that construct valuations from projected financial returns.  The juxtapositions of enthusiasm for impact investing and reticence to quantify social impact in the valuation process reflects the unease that financial professionals have paying for value flows that are more difficult to measure than capital and that development professionals have quantifying and monetizing value flows that have historically been qualitative measures of success.  The increasing standardization of social impact measurement methodology has provided the foundation for integrating social impact into an enterprise’s projection of future value flows and the recent financial crisis has provided opportunities for re-evaluating our mechanisms for measuring the risk and return, including pricing debt and equity based on the valuation of future value flows.  This paper identifies the issues involved in projecting, valuing, and pricing and creating financial instruments for blended value investments and proposes new models to tackle these issues, including a blended private cost of capital model that would price financial and social expected returns based on an industry average from relevant investors and a specific capital adjustment reflecting the alignment of an enterprise’s projected social impact and a fund’s social impact priorities.  Through the identification of issues and proposal of new models, this paper aims to stir debate among funders, academics, social entrepreneurs and impact measurement professional whose co-operation and co-ordination are necessary to achieve the goal of allocating capital according to an enterprise’s creation of total value.

I also perform month-end reconciliations, resolve exception reports, and support audit preparations by maintaining transparent and accurate records. In addition, I prepare benefit statements, trustee reports, and other documentation required for production management and compliance audits. My attention to detail, accuracy, and understanding of fund operations enable me to uphold high standards of financial integrity and administrative efficiency.

Beyond reconciliations and compliance, I manage a wide range of claims including withdrawal, retirement, death, divorce, funeral, disability, and dread disease claims — from verification and tax application to final payment. I work closely with SARS for tax directives and with investment teams to ensure the correct execution of investment and disinvestment mandates. My role also includes resolving member and client queries via email, phone, or in-person, ensuring professional and timely service delivery. By combining technical expertise with a strong commitment to accuracy, service, and compliance, I contribute to the effective administration of retirement funds while supporting both employer and member satisfaction. I am passionate about continuous professional growth within the financial services industry and remain committed to excellence, accountability, and delivering value through every aspect of fund administration.

about:
My Executive philosophy is simple: "Great businesses are built when strategy, people, innovation, technology and financial discipline work together."

I am a seasoned Business Executive, Business Strategist and Board Advisor with more than 25 years of leadership experience driving business growth, organisational transformation and operational excellence across Southern Africa. My executive career spans workforce solutions, business process outsourcing, management consulting, advisory, technology, logistics, manufacturing, financial services, telecommunications, retail and mining, automotive & fleet management solutions and where I consistently delivered sustainable commercial growth, strengthened governance and led complex business transformation initiatives. 

I currently serve as the Managing Director of Afrizan People Intelligence Pty Ltd (Temporary Employment Services) business and Omnetrix Pty Ltd (Functional Outsourcing), where I am responsible for corporate strategy, commercial growth, financial stewardship, governance, risk management and executive leadership. 

Throughout my career I have built businesses from start-up, led multi-million-rand operations, transformed underperforming divisions, modernised technology platforms and developed high-performing leadership teams across workforce solutions, business process outsourcing, consulting, logistics, manufacturing, telecommunications, financial services, fleet management, retail and mining.

I have extensive experience working with Boards, Executive Committees, shareholders, government stakeholders and strategic partners, providing leadership on growth strategy, governance, organisational transformation and long-term value creation. 

I serve on company boards, have advised the Minister of Labour and the Compensation Fund Commissioner, and a Lecturer in Business Leadership and Entrepreneurship at The Da Vinci Institute.

I am passionate about building organisations that are commercially successful, operationally disciplined, technologically enabled and people focused.

location.linkedinText: City of Cape Town, Western Cape, South Africa

about:
Mandela Washington Fellow (2023) and Mail & Guardian 200 Young South Africans, I work at the intersection of impact strategy, partnerships, and programme delivery, leading the design and implementation of initiatives that deliver measurable, long-term outcomes.

My experience spans South Africa, Botswana, Zambia, Zimbabwe, the US, and the UK, where I work with corporates, foundations, and community partners to align strategy, stakeholders, and delivery across complex, multi-stakeholder environments.

I lead across the full project lifecycle — from programme design and stakeholder engagement to implementation, operations, and impact reporting — with a strong focus on execution, sustainability, and scale. My background in finance strengthens my approach to planning, resourcing, and operational oversight.

Alongside this, I bring experience in resource mobilisation, securing and managing international funding to support programme delivery and long-term sustainability.

I am also the Founding Director of Girls With Wiings, where I have grown the organisation into a sustainable, community-based programme supporting over 600 women each month through menstrual health and economic empowerment initiatives.

I am particularly interested in building practical, scalable solutions that are grounded in the realities of the communities they serve.

publications.title: Going Green in Public Facilities report
Energy Services Market Intelligence Report
publications.description:
The 2016 Energy Services (ES) Market Intelligence Report contains energy efficiency and embedded generation market related  information. Previously, energy efficiency (EE) and embedded generation (EG) have been viewed separately, but the market is consolidating with the same players looking at both sides of the energy coin. Therefore we can now define energy services as services that are delivering demand- and/or supply-side solutions to energy users. This report provides an overview of this evolving market in South Africa, including the value chain, key players, policies and regulation as well as key opportunities and barriers.

Key opportunities highlighted include energy service opportunities in municipal wastewater treatment work facilities, public buildings as well as key changes to policies that will impact on the growth of the ES market in South Africa in 2016.

about:
What if your leadership excellence was matched by financial confidence that creates generational wealth? 
That's the transformation I facilitate every day.
With my Chartered Accountant designation and two decades in the financial sector, I have seen firsthand how women leaders transform their communities when they master their finances. As the author of "Master Your Finances: The Art of Building Wealth" and "The Oil, the Gift, and the Talent," I combine deep financial expertise with practical coaching that creates real results.

My work sits at the intersection of three powerful forces: leadership development, personal finance, and the unique opportunities emerging for Africans. Whether you are an entrepreneur, early career, mid-career professional ready to build wealth or a senior leader mentoring the next generation, I provide the strategies, accountability, and community support to make it happen.

Beyond the balance sheets and strategic plans, I am anchored by what matters most, my roles as wife, mother, aunt, sister, friend, coach, advisor and mentor. These relationships remind me daily why financial freedom matters: it's not just about numbers, it's about the impact we create and the legacy we leave.

For over 20 years, I have inspired and empowered hundreds of women to enhance their lives, finances, careers, and businesses.

Let's connect if you're ready to: Build wealth that reflects your worth • Develop leadership skills that inspire change • Create financial strategies rooted in faith and purpose.

headline: Managing Director at Merchant Capital South Africa

location.linkedinText: City of Johannesburg, Gauteng, South Africa

about:
I'm a creative engineer, who is driven by business growth and results. Yes the profile is Wealth Dynamics, but the most accurate short description of how I work. I build things and I fix things, and I bring strategic thinking to both.
  
For the last eight years I've been at Merchant Capital - an innovative South African SME FinTech – I have focused on revenue. However, the way I deliver on revenue growth is through building the business model that makes it happen. That means owning the direct revenue functions: sales, retentions, partnerships and marketing, while working on the go-to-market strategy, channel mix, market positioning, conversion, client retention and the operating model and infrastructure which makes revenue and margin growth possible. I like business cases and considered thinking, but also quick to make decisions where the path is trial-and-error, but absolutely clear as high potential. 
  
In practice that means understanding how we best go to market: which channels, which messages, what the team needs to execute. I use data to tell the story of what's working and what isn't, and to make better commercial decisions. I bring the team together around data, their feedback and client feedback to adjust targeting, diagnose blockages and solve problems. I give my team the direction, structure, space and tools, so they can use their strengths, take their own approach, with absolute leeway to experiment and to run things.
  
Before Merchant Capital, I spent around 15 years in business and corporate banking across South Africa and Africa and consulted in African markets on go-to-market strategy for financial services clients navigating complex environments. I also ran a small business, which gave me direct SME business experience — something that genuinely informs how I think about our clients. Merchant Capital is one of the highlights of my career: working with innovative, agile, entrepreneurial people in a phenomenal business, where I have a material part to play in its growth.

An equal focus on strategy and execution: the real work is building what’s needed - the commercial infrastructure to scale, frameworks, team capability and alignment across product, tech and commercial that turns strategy into a business that delivers. This includes improving sales conversion, scaling channels and strengthening the client proposition. A data-driven approach throughout covering operational, revenue and performance reporting with root cause analysis to find the ‘why’ for blockages, and then solve it.

projects.title: A new way of working for a Pan-African bank's marketing team
projects.description: A South African bank had transformed their marketing strategy but found execution was delayed due to existing silos and entrenched methods for delivering marketing initiatives. The Genesis senior Financial Services team considered various alternatives and based on a good understanding of the market and internal dynamics, proposed an innovative ‘way of working’ which overlaid the current bank structure and reporting lines. The proposal was work-shopped with the bank marketing team to determine the practicalities and principles of implementation and areas to pilot the new approach.

projects.title: A unique value proposition for younger bank customers in Namibia
projects.description: A bank in Namibia was struggling to attract the young high-potential customers in a small and highly competitive market. I provided oversight to the project and ensured client expectations were understood and met. The team delivered an excellent outcome, with the client kick-starting execution through building product capability.

projects.title: Strategy review for the Board of a local Ugandan Bank
projects.description: Genesis advised the Board and the Executive on strategy and execution changes needed to meet financial targets and sustainable growth. Our assessment of the evolving market needs, competition and mobile and regulatory developments in the banking sector underpinned our advice. Genesis developed a financial model based on the market opportunity and related bank balance sheet and income statement impact over a three year period to substantiate our findings. Our work honed the bank's strategic objectives, enabled the bank to re-prioritise activities accordingly, and set sustainable and realistic targets with the Board.

projects.title: A cost allocation model which ensures better decision making for a large South African Bank
projects.description: The Genesis team developed a cost recovery model for the Shared Services Division, based on activity based costing principles.  Genesis developed a model which bridged front office and shared services, working closely with Business, Costing and Finance to allocate costs based on resources and effort, using new ways of looking at the available data sources. The model, which was accepted as business-logical and driving the right behaviour and decisions, was implemented by the bank.

projects.title: Facilitation of an Exco-Board strategy day for a bank in Botswana
projects.description: Building on the strategy refresh conducted in 2015 by Genesis, I was asked to facilitate an Exco-Board workshop so as to achieve strategy and budget sign-off. The MD and Executive took the Board through the key points while I facilitated the discussion and posed relevant questions for the Board and Exco to debate.

projects.title: Investment Banking demand side analysis for 14 countries in Sub-Saharan Africa
projects.description: The Investment Banking division of a Pan-African bank wanted to plan for allocation of balance sheet, people and skills across its key African geographies for a three year period. Genesis defined the market opportunity and the bank's market position. We provided a consolidated demand-side analysis, including a macro, sector and capital market maturity trend analysis.  Added to this we analysed the bank's current market share per country across all Investment Banking products, including equity, debt instruments and term lending. Together with the bank's in-country budgets, forecasts and growth plans, this report was used by Investment Banking to validate allocation of resources.

projects.title: Linking an African bank's Corporate & Investment Banking strategic initiatives to budgets
projects.description: Genesis worked with the Corporate & Investment Banking Regional Head to link initiatives and client sales to budgets - graphically for monthly tracking. This was then tested and used by the executive in specific countries to measure progress against targets, create clear accountability and enable early corrective action.

projects.title: A top tier Namibian bank's market position and strategy execution plan
projects.description: The primary requirement of this top tier bank was the development of an execution plan across functions, with management buy-in, based on an existing three-year strategy. We also provided an outside-in view of the bank - an analysis of the bank's market position and feedback from customers - to position the strategy. The Genesis team worked across front-line business units and support functions to synthesise objectives and plans to deliver on the strategy. We helped to design and facilitate a 250 people strong managers' conference where feedback was obtained and used as input into the final work-plan prioritisation. The final deliverable was an interactive, self-explanatory initiatives work-book, across all areas of the bank.  This tracking tool was adopted by the Executive Committee to maintain alignment and ensure on-going measurement against targets.

projects.title: Embedding a Retail Banking strategy in Malawi through execution and monitoring
projects.description: The Retail Banking arm of a universal bank in Malawi was looking to solidify their strategy, embed this within the organisation and develop an implementation plan which tracked progress and measurable targets. I worked with senior management to clarify Retail Banking's role in delivering the bank's sustainability and profitability targets. Myself and the Genesis Analytics' team reviewed the bank's financial 'shape', its financial position in relation to its peers and the macroeconomic environment. We then conducted a client needs assessment, highlighting where the banks' Client Value Proposition required refinement, capability builds or re-positioning in the market. The engagement culminated in a three-day strategy workshop with the Retail Banking management team where the Genesis Analytics team's work was used to deepen the Retail Banking strategy for the year. During the work-shop, we facilitated the development of an implementation plan for Retail Banking as well as support functions. The final deliverable included an interactive initiative-tracking tool which was adopted by the Executive to monitor and report on initiative measures, dependencies and red flags.

projects.title: Bank Marketing-Agency operating model and Marketing measurement dashboard
projects.description: To optimise spend, and improve execution and measurement of Marketing effectiveness and efficiency, Genesis Analytics developed the Marketing-Agency operating model in conjunction with Group Marketing, the Lead Agency and country Marketing Departments in Africa. We also developed a macro-driven dashboard which included metrics related to financial, operational, efficiency and effectiveness measures, with the audience being Marketing Departments in Africa and Head Office, Business Partners and the Agency.  Agency measures were incorporated into the new SLAs set up with the lead agency and local agencies, to support the lead and local agency model.  We also assisted in developing an operating model and measurement execution plan with Group Marketing.

projects.title: A Pan-African bank requires a mid-term strategy review in Uganda
projects.description: A universal bank in Uganda continued to struggle in delivering on their five-year strategy - in a tough market with aggressive internal profitability targets. The Genesis team was able to clearly define the areas of opportunity for the bank, considering the macro and competitive environment and customer insights. We also identified the gaps in offering, capabilities and positioning, and how to close the gaps.  Our approach was highly interactive and concluded with a workshop of the full management team on the execution plan.

projects.title: Insurance/ Investment House business model regulatory review
projects.description: Genesis Analytics provided an opinion to a South African Insurance & Investment Management Institution looking to respond proactively to regulatory change.  I provided oversight to the work, primarily formulated by Mauro, which also provided recommendations to enhance the appropriateness of the business model in anticipation of the expected content of upcoming reforms.

projects.title: Measurement dashboard creation for a bank's Mobile Business Unit
projects.description: The Mobile Business Unit's executive of a large African bank needed to measure and monitor, as close to real time as possible, the adoption and usage of the new mobile and tablet app launched into the market. I led the Genesis Analytics team in developing a configurable dashboard, with measures and analytics agreed and stress tested with the executive, covering adoption and usage to operational performance.

projects.title: Bank digital channels adoption uptake through improved market understanding
projects.description: For the Digital team of a Pan-African bank, I brought together Genesis Analytics’ customer profiling capability, customer digital behaviour analytics plus market sizing assessment in order to ascertain the bank’s mobile app market size for a five year period. Mobile device and operating system trends where taken into account to predict the market size across various variables, including customer profiles, geography and technologies, and targets were recommended for adoption over time.

projects.title: Optimising Marketing spend of a large Pan-African bank
projects.description: I led an engagement with the Global Marketing Department of a large Pan-African bank, tackling the requirement to improve spend efficiency management, taking both metric capability and the Global Lead Agency Model into account. This entailed an analysis across five African countries and the development of recommendations related to the Bank-Agency operating model, efficiency gains in processes and capability as well as metrics required to demonstrate success to product houses.

projects.title: Scenario planning for the retail vehicle financing division of a Top Tier South African bank
projects.description: A large South African bank sought a review of their vehicle financing strategy to determine a course of action which would optimise Return on Equity.  The Genesis Analytics team completed a macro, competitor and industry analysis, together with a deep quantitative customer analysis to set the parameters for the scenario planning. Based on this, scenarios were modelled ranging from shut down to aggressively taking on the market, identifying key strategic decisions to be made and recommending a five year course of action.

projects.title: Strategic due diligence of a Tier 3 microfinance bank in Kenya
projects.description: I led the business development, product and sales capability analysis stream on a commercial due diligence involving a tier 3 microfinance bank in Kenya.  This involved assessing the bank’s ability to grow its customer base and attract liabilities based on its current value proposition, together with an assessment of the bank’s product, service and channel strategy.

about:
PHD registered , Masters in Financial Engineering.
Academic qualifications have been further enhanced by hands-on experience  with time spent at financial giants like Deutsche Bank, HSBC, Bear Stearns, and JP Morgan in London.

At JP Morgan London, I spearheaded  intricate portfolio structures, a notable one being the Municipal structuring for the city of London, which spanned over GBP 1 billion. Tenure as a senior derivatives sales trader at Nedbank Capital in South Africa was marked by significant contributions in creating and shaping equity and derivative products and portfolios.

My dexterity in the realm of finance isn't just limited to portfolio management; I've also exhibited a keen aptitude in credit deal structuring and credit model design. This was particularly evident during my leadership role at Absa as the Head of Sales and Credit for its Technology Finance entity. I had the responsibility of managing a financial book worth R4 billion and played a central role in broadening the product horizon into Greater Africa.

I then took on the mantle as the Head of Sales for Business Core Banking at FNB. I was instrumental in laying down the foundations and spearheading a new sales division dedicated to meeting the requirements of the core transactional product house. This portfolio spanned transactional banking and credit, boasting an impressive value of over R5.5 billion NPAT.

In 2018, I ventured into a new frontier by launching my hedge fund and advisory consulting firm. My vision is crystal clear: to create a substantial positive impact on the lives of the common people, with a pronounced emphasis on alleviating poverty by addressing key thematic concerns. The cornerstone of my firm is Responsible Investing which entails both Resource Mobilization ( Capital Raising – Banks, DFI’s, Family Offices etc ) and Optimal Capital allocation ( listed and unlisted investments) in  ESG/ Climate Finance / Sustainability as well as Traditional assets. This spans PE, M&A, VC, ESD, Traditional Equity and Debt Capital Market solutioning, Project Finance and SME creation to lending. This business model is pivotal in achieving our ambitious goals of fostering job opportunities and fortifying a circular economy in South Africa.

I actively engage in financing energy projects, championing carbon footprint reduction, and endorsing the "just transition" paradigm. Beyond this, I  provide thought leadership on ESD/BEE and financing in the SME domain. This reflects my  commitment to fostering an economic growth trajectory that is both sustainable and inclusive.

headline: CEO @ Dass Capital Family Office | Buyouts of established South African businesses | Permanent capital, no exit deadlines.

location.linkedinText: Johannesburg Metropolitan Area

about:
Most investors ask: how do I get in, make a return, and get out?
 
That has never been my question.
 
I grew up around a family business built over 90 years, with the kind of long-term thinking most of the investment industry considers impractical.
 
When my family transitioned from operating businesses to managing capital, I brought that philosophy with me.
 
Through Dass Capital, our single family office, I make majority investments in established, owner-managed South African businesses. We invest the capital of one family, for the long term.
 
No fund. No external investors. No exit deadlines.
 
Most of the founders I meet are thinking about the next chapter. They have spent decades building something that works, and they want liquidity without watching it get dismantled.
 
Because we are never forced to sell what we buy, founders can retain a stake, keep good management in place, and step back on their own timeline.
 
What I look for:
• Profitable, established businesses with 5+ years of operating history
• Owner-managed, with succession or liquidity in view
• Strong management and culture worth preserving
• Alignment on what the business should become
 
We also run a specialist GP stakes practice, the first of its kind in South Africa, taking long-term minority positions in fund managers.
 
I write about long-term investing in my newsletter, Rule of Acquisition. I call my style Extraordinary Investing: I look for extraordinary businesses, not ordinary ones.
 
If you are a founder thinking about your next chapter, or an advisor with a mandate that fits, the conversation is confidential and there is no obligation on either side.
